topic:
Career and Identity Tradeoff

What should I do if the AI research track may be both highly resourced and increasingly fragile?
context:
I am 27. I did my undergrad at University of Toronto and I am doing a master's at MBZUAI. Both are in AI. I am currently on a research engineer / research scientist track.

I am worried about several things:

1. AI agents can already conduct parts of research. In a few years, there may be a trend where AI systems replace more than half of the papers published at top conferences.
2. The industry is getting more competitive. More importantly, people mainly compete for resources by publishing papers. That goal is being highly optimized by many players, which makes the work more specialized and possibly more vulnerable to replacement by AI.
3. I was diagnosed with ADHD. I find it difficult to stay on track under peer pressure, and I do not enjoy much of what is called "research" when academia starts valuing consistency more than novelty.
4. The chance of an AI bubble is getting bigger now. It looks a bit like the dot-com bubble era. What happens if capital stops flowing in and feeding the industry?
5. My advantage is system-level thinking across domains: philosophy, AI technology, cognitive science, economics, sociology, complex systems, and related areas. I write deep blog posts that synthesize these topics. I started to develop my own "narritive".

What should I do? Should I push myself a bit more to publish papers and get access to industry resources before everything changes, since there are still lots of resources in the AI industry? Or should I focus on my strengths: writing blogs, starting an influencer account, and trying business ideas?

The hard part is that I do not have a clear idea of what to do if I stop grinding papers, so the alternative path has a lot of uncertainty.
